notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; simulated R0, so there is no hardware backend and no hardware run was made. The package serves DroneHoverSimpleEnv-v0, the card's first entry symbol; the other hover, takeoff and circle entry symbols are named in facts.md but not packaged, and can be served by changing env_id, native, facts and fake. Package code never imports or runs the upstream clone (its setup.py:24-34 installs gymnasium, pybullet, numpy, torch and more), so the fake backend is the package's own pure Python implementation of the simplified hover equations (fake.py); the sim backend (gymnasium.make) was not run and the fake was not compared with the upstream PyBullet environment. The fake returns the full 34-value observation (two history entries of 13 observation plus 4 action values), not a smaller array. Five warnings are expected of this Gymnasium family driver: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only sets the pending seed for the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT on inputs the bridge derives (reset.seed, seed.seed, step.ticks, step.action.values[*]); the family bridge declares no units for those derived inputs and the package leaves the warnings. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning occurred. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. Not covered: the other entry symbols, the sim backend, observation noise, the 10% domain randomization, contacts, drag, ground effect, motor dynamics and any upstream comparison. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
